data.source_title: ACR Appropriateness Criteria®: Acute Hand and Wrist Trauma
data.locator: Variant 1: Suspect acute hand or wrist trauma, initial imaging; Variant 2: initial radiographs negative or equivocal, next imaging study; narrative pages 3–5
data.source_setting: Acute hand/wrist trauma imaging decision support; suspected adult wrist fracture case is within scope, though recommendations cover broader ages and hand injuries.
value: For suspected acute hand/wrist trauma, initial radiographs of the area of interest are usually appropriate.

If initial radiographs are negative or equivocal but clinical suspicion persists, ACR lists repeat radiographs in 10–14 days, noncontrast CT, or noncontrast MRI as usually appropriate next imaging options.
data.source_evidence_basis: The ACR Appropriateness Criteria narrative’s Variant 1 rates radiography as usually appropriate for suspected acute hand/wrist trauma. Variant 2 lists repeat radiographs, CT without IV contrast, and MRI without IV contrast as usually appropriate after negative/equivocal radiographs.
data.limitations: Imaging appropriateness guidance does not determine individual immobilization, reduction, referral, or discharge; the repeat-radiograph option may delay diagnosis. Do not infer fracture absence from a negative initial study when suspicion remains.
data.inferred_scenario_use: Model initial assessment and radiographs, then branch by result and continuing clinician suspicion to follow-up imaging or other locally approved care.
data.applicability: Acute trauma with suspected wrist/hand injury; adapt to patient age, examination, pregnancy status, and local imaging/referral pathways.
data.source_period: ACR narrative identifies the topic as revised in 2018; whether superseded or reaffirmed is not stated on the accessed narrative (retrieved 2026-10-10).
data.source_n: Not applicable; guideline/pathway, not a patient cohort
data.role_assignment_basis: Role participants are proposed scenario assignments inferred from the pathway setting for simulation design; the cited source does not enumerate this exact role list.
